topic: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Screening: men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked
population: men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked
description: The USPSTF recommends 1-time screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) with ultrasonography in men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked.

topic: Anxiety Disorders in Adults: Screening: adults 64 years or younger, including pregnant and postpartum persons
population: adults 64 years or younger, including pregnant and postpartum persons
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for anxiety disorders in adults, including pregnant and postpartum persons.

topic: Anxiety in Children and Adolescents: Screening: children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years
population: children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for anxiety in children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years.

topic: Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication: pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia
population: pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia
description: The USPSTF recommends the use of low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) as preventive medication after 12 weeks of gestation in persons who are at high risk for preeclampsia. See the Practice Considerations section for information on high risk and aspirin dose.

topic: Asymptomatic Bacteriuria in Adults: Screening: pregnant persons
population: pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for asymptomatic bacteriuria using urine culture in pregnant persons.

topic: BRCA-Related Cancer: Risk Assessment, Genetic Counseling, and Genetic Testing: women with a personal or family history of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer or an ancestry associated with brca1/2 gene mutation
population: women with a personal or family history of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer or an ancestry associated with brca1/2 gene mutation
description: The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians assess women with a personal or family history of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer or who have an ancestry associated with breast cancer susceptibility 1 and 2 (BRCA1/2) gene mutations with an appropriate brief familial risk assessment tool. Women with a positive result on the risk assessment tool should receive genetic counseling and, if indicated after counseling, genetic testing.

topic: Breast Cancer: Medication Use to Reduce Risk: women at increased risk for breast cancer aged 35 years or older
population: women at increased risk for breast cancer aged 35 years or older
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer to prescribe risk-reducing medications, such as tamoxifen, raloxifene, or aromatase inhibitors, to women who are at increased risk for breast cancer and at low risk for adverse medication effects.

topic: Breast Cancer: Screening: women aged 40 to 74 years
population: women aged 40 to 74 years
description: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years. †

topic: Breastfeeding: Primary Care Behavioral Counseling Interventions: pregnant and postpartum women
population: pregnant and postpartum women
description: The USPSTF recommends providing interventions or referrals, during pregnancy and after birth, to support breastfeeding.

topic: Cervical Cancer: Screening: women aged 21 to 65 years
population: women aged 21 to 65 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for cervical cancer every 3 years with cervical cytology alone in women aged 21 to 29 years. For women aged 30 to 65 years, the USPSTF recommends screening every 3 years with cervical cytology alone, every 5 years with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing alone, or every 5 years with hrHPV testing in combination with cytology (cotesting). See the Clinical Considerations section for the relative benefits and harms of alternative screening strategies for women 21 years or older.

topic: Chlamydia and Gonorrhea: Screening: sexually active women, including pregnant persons
population: sexually active women, including pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for gonorrhea in all sexually active women 24 years or younger and in women 25 years or older who are at increased risk for infection.

topic: Chlamydia and Gonorrhea: Screening: sexually active women, including pregnant persons
population: sexually active women, including pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for chlamydia in all sexually active women 24 years or younger and in women 25 years or older who are at increased risk for infection.

topic: Colorectal Cancer: Screening: adults aged 45 to 49 years
population: adults aged 45 to 49 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in adults aged 45 to 49 years. See the "Practice Considerations" section and Table 1 for details about screening strategies.

topic: Colorectal Cancer: Screening: adults aged 50 to 75 years
population: adults aged 50 to 75 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 50 to 75 years. See the "Practice Considerations" section and Table 1 for details about screening strategies.

topic: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening: adults, including pregnant and postpartum persons, and older adults (65 years or older)
population: adults, including pregnant and postpartum persons, and older adults (65 years or older)
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons, as well as older adults.

topic: Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: Screening: adolescents aged 12 to 18 years
population: adolescents aged 12 to 18 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for major depressive disorder (MDD) in adolescents aged 12 to 18 years.

topic: Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions: community-dwelling adults 65 years or older
population: community-dwelling adults 65 years or older
description: The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults 65 years or older who are at increased risk for falls.

topic: Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects: Preventive Medication: persons who plan to or could become pregnant
population: persons who plan to or could become pregnant
description: The USPSTF recommends that all persons planning to or who could become pregnant take a daily supplement containing 0.4 to 0.8 mg (400 to 800 mcg) of folic acid.

topic: Gestational Diabetes: Screening: asymptomatic pregnant persons at 24 weeks of gestation or after
population: asymptomatic pregnant persons at 24 weeks of gestation or after
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for gestational diabetes in asymptomatic pregnant persons at 24 weeks of gestation or after.

topic: Healthy Diet and Physical Activity for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors: Behavioral Counseling Interventions: adults with cardiovascular disease risk factors
population: adults with cardiovascular disease risk factors
description: The USPSTF recommends offering or referring adults with cardiovascular disease risk factors to behavioral counseling interventions to promote a healthy diet and physical activity.

topic: Healthy Weight and Weight Gain In Pregnancy: Behavioral Counseling Interventions: pregnant persons
population: pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer pregnant persons effective behavioral counseling interventions aimed at promoting healthy weight gain and preventing excess gestational weight gain in pregnancy.

topic: Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening: adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection
population: adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection. See the Practice Considerations section for a description of adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection.

topic: Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Pregnant Women: Screening: pregnant women
population: pregnant women
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in pregnant women at their first prenatal visit

topic: Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening: adults aged 18 to 79 years
population: adults aged 18 to 79 years
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults aged 18 to 79 years.

topic: High Body Mass Index in Children and Adolescents: Interventions: children and adolescents 6 years or older
population: children and adolescents 6 years or older
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians provide or refer children and adolescents 6 years or older with a high body mass index (BMI) (≥95th percentile for age and sex) to comprehensive, intensive behavioral interventions. See the Practice Considerations section for more information about behavioral interventions.

topic: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection: Screening: adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years
population: adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for HIV infection in adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years. Younger adolescents and older adults who are at increased risk of infection should also be screened. See the Clinical Considerations section for more information about assessment of risk, screening intervals, and rescreening in pregnancy.

topic: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection: Screening: pregnant persons
population: pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for HIV infection in all pregnant persons, including those who present in labor or at delivery whose HIV status is unknown.

topic: Hypertension in Adults: Screening: adults 18 years or older without known hypertension
population: adults 18 years or older without known hypertension
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertension in adults 18 years or older with office blood pressure measurement (OBPM). The USPSTF recommends obtaining blood pressure measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment.

topic: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: Screening: asymptomatic pregnant persons
population: asymptomatic pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertensive disorders in pregnant persons with blood pressure measurements throughout pregnancy.

topic: Intimate Partner Violence and Caregiver Abuse of Older or Vulnerable Adults: Screening: women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum women
population: women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum women
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for intimate partner violence (IPV) in women of reproductive age, including those who are pregnant and postpartum. See the "Practice Considerations" section for information on evidence-based multicomponent interventions and for information on IPV in men.

topic: Latent Tuberculosis Infection in Adults: Screening: asymptomatic adults at increased risk of latent tuberculosis infection (ltbi)
population: asymptomatic adults at increased risk of latent tuberculosis infection (ltbi)
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for LTBI in populations at increased risk. See the "Assessment of Risk" section for additional information on adults at increased risk.

topic: Lung Cancer: Screening: adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years
population: adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years
description: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years. Screening should be discontinued once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that substantially limits life expectancy or the ability or willingness to have curative lung surgery.

topic: Ocular Prophylaxis for Gonococcal Ophthalmia Neonatorum: Preventive Medication: newborns
population: newborns
description: The USPSTF recommends prophylactic ocular topical medication for all newborns to prevent gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum.

topic: Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: Screening: postmenopausal women younger than 65 years with 1 or more risk factors for osteoporosis
population: postmenopausal women younger than 65 years with 1 or more risk factors for osteoporosis
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women younger than 65 years who are at increased risk for an osteoporotic fracture as estimated by clinical risk assessment. See the "Practice Considerations" section for more information on risk assessment and screening tests.

topic: Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: Screening: women 65 years or older
population: women 65 years or older
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in women 65 years or older. See the "Practice Considerations" section for more information on screening tests.

topic: Perinatal Depression: Preventive Interventions: pregnant and postpartum persons
population: pregnant and postpartum persons
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians provide or refer pregnant and postpartum persons who are at increased risk of perinatal depression to counseling interventions.

topic: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening: asymptomatic adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity
population: asymptomatic adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Clinicians should offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.

topic: Prevention of Acquisition of HIV: Preexposure Prophylaxis: adolescents and adults at increased risk of hiv
population: adolescents and adults at increased risk of hiv
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe preexposure prophylaxis using effective antiretroviral therapy to persons who are at increased risk of HIV acquisition to decrease the risk of acquiring HIV. See the Practice Considerations section for more information about identification of persons at increased risk and about effective antiretroviral therapy.

topic: Prevention of Dental Caries in Children Younger Than 5 Years: Screening and Interventions: children younger than 5 years
population: children younger than 5 years
description: The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians apply fluoride varnish to the primary teeth of all infants and children starting at the age of primary tooth eruption.

topic: Prevention of Dental Caries in Children Younger Than 5 Years: Screening and Interventions: children younger than 5 years
population: children younger than 5 years
description: The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians prescribe oral fluoride supplementation starting at age 6 months for children whose water supply is deficient in fluoride.

topic: Rh(D) Incompatibility: Screening: pregnant women, during the first pregnancy-related care visit
population: pregnant women, during the first pregnancy-related care visit
description: The USPSTF strongly recommends Rh(D) blood typing and antibody testing for all pregnant women during their first visit for pregnancy-related care.

topic: Rh(D) Incompatibility: Screening: unsensitized rh(d)-negative pregnant women
population: unsensitized rh(d)-negative pregnant women
description: The USPSTF recommends repeated Rh(D) antibody testing for all unsensitized Rh(D)-negative women at 24 to 28 weeks' gestation, unless the biological father is known to be Rh(D)-negative.

topic: Sexually Transmitted Infections: Behavioral Counseling: sexually active adolescents and adults at increased risk
population: sexually active adolescents and adults at increased risk
description: The USPSTF recommends behavioral counseling for all sexually active adolescents and for adults who are at increased risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs). See the Practice Considerations section for more information on populations at increased risk for acquiring STIs.

topic: Skin Cancer Prevention: Behavioral Counseling: young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children
population: young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children
description: The USPSTF recommends counseling young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation for persons aged 6 months to 24 years with fair skin types to reduce their risk of skin cancer.

topic: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication: adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more cardiovascular risk factors and an estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease (cvd) risk of 10% or greater
population: adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more cardiovascular risk factors and an estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease (cvd) risk of 10% or greater
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe a statin for the primary prevention of CVD for adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more CVD risk factors (i.e. dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking) and an estimated 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event of 10% or greater.

topic: Syphilis Infection During Pregnancy: Screening: asymptomatic pregnant women
population: asymptomatic pregnant women
description: The USPSTF recommends early, universal screening for syphilis infection during pregnancy; if an individual is not screened early in pregnancy, the USPSTF recommends screening at the first available opportunity.

topic: Syphilis Infection in Nonpregnant Adolescents and Adults: Screening: asymptomatic, nonpregnant adolescents and adults who are at increased risk for syphilis infection
population: asymptomatic, nonpregnant adolescents and adults who are at increased risk for syphilis infection
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for syphilis infection in persons who are at increased risk for infection.

topic: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions: nonpregnant adults
population: nonpregnant adults
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all adults about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)--approved pharmacotherapy for cessation to nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.

topic: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions: pregnant persons
population: pregnant persons
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all pregnant persons about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions for cessation to pregnant persons who use tobacco.

topic: Tobacco Use in Children and Adolescents: Primary Care Interventions: school-aged children and adolescents who have not started to use tobacco
population: school-aged children and adolescents who have not started to use tobacco
description: The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians provide interventions, including education or brief counseling, to prevent initiation of tobacco use among school-aged children and adolescents.

topic: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions: adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women
population: adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women
description: The USPSTF recommends screening for unhealthy alcohol use in primary care settings in adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women, and providing persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions to reduce unhealthy alcohol use.

topic: Unhealthy Drug Use: Screening: adults age 18 years or older
population: adults age 18 years or older
description: The USPSTF recommends screening by asking questions about unhealthy drug use in adults age 18 years or older. Screening should be implemented when services for accurate diagnosis, effective treatment, and appropriate care can be offered or referred. (Screening refers to asking questions about unhealthy drug use, not testing biological specimens.)

topic: Vision in Children Ages 6 Months to 5 Years: Screening: children aged 3 to 5 years
population: children aged 3 to 5 years
description: The USPSTF recommends vision screening at least once in all children aged 3 to 5 years to detect amblyopia or its risk factors.

topic: Weight Loss to Prevent Obesity-Related Morbidity and Mortality in Adults: Behavioral Interventions: adults
population: adults
description: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer or refer adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher (calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) to intensive, multicomponent behavioral interventions.
